units.title: Offer a clear next step that names the tangible outcome for the audience

claim.text: The exercise is to identify the clear and attractive next step offered to the audience and to name the tangible, meaningful outcome the audience takes away, not just a bare request.
claim.quote: So the exercise is what's the clear and attractive next step that you offer your audience?

action.text: Define what you will offer the audience on the website so they actually want to become a lead, and state what they will take away (for example, a free consultation plus we will help you X).
action.quote: It has to be request a free consultation and we will help you X.

args.text: A call to action that is a meaningless step with no perceived value to the visitor.
args.quote: It's a meaningless step for me. There's no perceived value of getting to that place.

args.text: A generic request for a free consultation without a stated outcome is not sufficient because there is no perceived value.
args.quote: It's not just, hey, request a free consultation because there's no perceived value there either.

unknowns: The source does not state how to measure whether the named outcome is attractive enough.

units.title: Check that the call to action moves people closer to their goals, specifically

claim.text: After defining the offer, the next question to ask is how it moves people closer to their goals, and the description must be very specific; if you cannot describe how it moves people closer to their goals, it is not compelling enough.
claim.quote: The next question to ask is, how does this move them closer to their goals? And we want to be really, really specific. If you can't describe how your lure, how your call to action actually moves people closer to their goals, it's not compelling enough.

action.text: Describe specifically how the call to action moves the audience closer to their goals; if it does not, treat it as not good enough yet and make it more compelling.
action.quote: And if it doesn't move them closer to their goals, it's not a good call. It's not a good enough call to action yet.

args.text: A call to action / lure has already been defined.
args.quote: So once you've done that, the next question to ask is, how does this move them closer to their goals?

unknowns: No standard or threshold for what counts as specific enough is given.

units.title: Reframe existing sales-process steps as the free offer instead of adding new steps

claim.text: The source says it is not about adding additional steps to the sales process but about reframing steps you already have, being very clear about the perceived value for people; the exhibition stand company was already doing free 3D visuals but was not selling that on the website.
claim.quote: We're not talking about adding additional steps into your sales process here. We're talking about reframing the steps that you already have so that we're being very clear about what the perceived value is for people.

action.text: Position an existing step (such as a 30-minute inquiry call or an already-provided free 3D visual) as the stated benefit of contacting you, rather than creating a new offer.
action.quote: they weren't advertising that that was a benefit of the consultation. So, they weren't getting as many leads as they could.

args.text: The business already delivers something of value at an existing step but does not advertise it as the benefit of inquiring.
args.quote: They just weren't selling it on the website.

args.text: There is an existing sales process step whose value can be reframed.
args.quote: So, you had to just make an inquiry and then, oh, you got this free 3D visual

unknowns: The source does not state how the reframing is executed on the website beyond advertising the benefit.

units.title: The worry about giving too much away is raised and addressed by reframing

claim.text: People worry about giving too much away, citing the cost of building free 3D stand visuals or doing free consultations, and not wanting to do so until someone is a client.
claim.quote: one of the things that people worry about here is they worry about giving too much away.

args.text: A business objects to free offers on the basis of cost or waiting until someone is a client.
args.quote: We don't want to do that until we know someone's a client.

unknowns: The source does not resolve the cost objection with numbers or a rule; it responds by asking to walk through the sales process.

units.title: Answer first-step objections on the website so visitors will act

claim.text: There is an objection type at the first step, inertia to act: unless a certain number of questions are answered and all the visitor's red flags are answered, they will not attempt to contact you, become an inquiry, buy, or sign up.
claim.quote: And that is this first step, inertia to act.

action.text: Answer the objections to the requested action right away on the page so visitors on the edge will act.
action.quote: We're targeting the people who are on the edge who don't know whether they want to buy from you or a competitor. And we need to answer these objections right away.

args.text: Visitors land on the page with unanswered questions and do not attempt any conversion action.
args.quote: unless they have a certain number of questions answered, they're not even going to attempt to contact you, become an inquiry, buy a first purchase, sign up for the newsletter, or anything like that.

args.text: There is a specific next step or form being offered to convert visitors.
args.quote: Otherwise, giving them this free quote form is pointless because a large percentage of them are going to say, "I have no way of knowing if this is the right thing for me at all."

unknowns: The source does not enumerate which questions must be answered for any given page or how many suffice.

units.title: Construction company free quote page as a wash-out example

claim.text: On a construction company page offering a free quote for architecture or building services, you would not know that from the page; request a free quote is a reasonable lure but presented this way it is a wash out given the uncertainty in the visitor's head.
claim.quote: You would not know that from this page.

args.text: A call to action button gives no description of the outcome or what will happen.
args.quote: But this at the moment, how this is prevent presented is a wash out because you think about all the uncertainty that you have in your head when you see this. Request a free quote.

unknowns: Whether the company changed the page is not stated.
The source does not state results or measurements from the suggested change.

units.title: Cycling accident claims: start my claim is too high commitment

claim.text: On a cycling accident claims page, the start my claim button is a complete wash out because it asks people to do too much and the objections to doing that thing are not handled; find out if you could claim, or find out how much you could claim, would be better.
claim.quote: the button is a complete wash out because it's asking people to do too much and they haven't handled the objections to doing that thing.

args.text: The visitor does not know whether they have a claim and will not start a claim in case there is a cost or embarrassment.
args.quote: start my claim is too high commitment. I don't know if I've got a claim and what I'm not going to do is just start my claim anyway in case there is cost to me

units.title: Target people on the edge, not those already ready to buy

claim.text: Only the most gung-ho people or those who already know they want to do business will put their details in, and for those people you do not need to worry about conversion optimization; the target is people on the edge who do not know whether to buy from you or a competitor.
claim.quote: it's only the most very gung-ho of people who are just going to stick in their details or it's the people that already know they want to do business with you. And for those guys, you don't need to worry about conversion optimization at all.

units.title: Brownies with cocktail sticks: social convention signals permission

claim.text: In the analogy, cocktail sticks in brownies signal by social convention that you may take one for free without being challenged.
claim.quote: we know that we are supposed to take one of those and we know that that's going to be free of charge. No one's going to come around the counter and shout at us for eating the food from the counter.

claim.quote: Now most people are familiar with objection handling in the sales process.

args.text: This unit is about objections to requesting the offer, not objections to doing business with you.

claim.quote: on the one hand Shinobi has this goal that he really really wants to get which is whatever your product or service delivers for him and then on the other hand he's got this fear doubt and uncertainty which is kind of weighing him down and preventing him from making that decision.
